source_text: Θαυμάζω δὲ, πῶς Ὀδρύσας μὲν καὶ Σαμόθρᾳκας καὶ Ἐλευσινίους καὶ Ὑπερβορέους ἐν τοῖς ἀρχαιοτάτοις καὶ σοφωτάτοις ἔταξεν ἔθνεσιν ὁ Κέλσος, τοὺς δὲ Ἰουδαίους οὐκ ἠξίωσεν οὔτε εἰς σοφοὺς παραδέξασθαι οὔτε εἰς ἀρχαίους· πολλῶν φερομένων συγγραμμάτων παρὰ Αἰγυπτίοις καὶ Φοίνιξι καὶ Ἕλλησι, μαρτυρούντων αὐτῶν τῇ ἀρχαιότητι, ἅπερ ἐγὼ περισσὸν ἡγησάμην εἶναι παραθέσθαι. δυνατὸν γὰρ τὸν βουλόμενον ἀναγνῶναι τὰ γεγραμμένα Φλαυίῳ Ἰωσήπῳ περὶ τῆς τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀρχαιότητος ἐν δυσὶν, ὅπου πολλὴν συναγωγὴν συγγραφέων φέρει μαρτυρούντων τῇ Ἰουδαίων ἀρχαιότητι. καὶ Τατιανοῦ δὲ νεωτέρου φέρεται ὁ πρὸς Ἕλληνας λόγος. πολυμαθέστατα ἐκτιθεμένου τοὺς ἱστορήσαντας περὶ τῆς Ἰουδαίων καὶ Μωϋσέως ἀρχαιότητος. ἔοικεν οὖν οὐκ ἀληθῶς ἀλλὰ φιλαπεχθημόνως ὁ Κέλσος ταῦτα λέγειν, σκοπὸν ἔχων κατηγορῆσαι τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ χριστιανισμοῦ. ἠρτημένης ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων. ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς μὲν Ὁμήρου Γαλακτοφάγους καὶ τοὺς Γαλατῶν Δρυΐδας καὶ τοὺς Γέτας σοφώτατα λέγει ἔθνη εἶναι καὶ ἀρχαῖα, περὶ τῶν συγγενῶν τοῖς Ἰουδαϊκοῖς λόγοις διαλαμβάνοντας. ὧν οὐκ οἶδα εἰ φέρεται συγγράμματα· Ἑβραίους δὲ μόνον τὸ ὅσον ἐφ᾿ ἑαυτῷ ἐκβάλλει καὶ τῆς ἀρχαιότητος καὶ τῆς σοφίας. πάλιν τε αὖ κατάλογον ποιούμενος ἀνδρῶν ἀρχαίων καὶ σοφῶν. ὠφελησάντων τοὺς κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς καὶ διὰ συγγραμμάτων τοὺς μετ᾿ αὐτοὺς, Μωϋσέα ἐξέβαλε τοῦ καταλόγου τῶν σοφῶν. καὶ Λίνου μὲν. ὃν προέταξεν ὧν ὠνόμασεν ὁ Κέλσος, οὔτε νόμοι οὔτε λόγοι φέρονται ἐπιστρέψαντες καὶ θεραπεύσαντες ἔθνη· Μωϋσέως δὲ τοὺς νόμους ὅλον ἔθνος φέρει ἐπεσπαρμένον τῇ πάσῃ οἰκουμένῃ. ὅρα οὖν εἰ μὴ αντικρυς κακουργῶν ἐξέβαλε τοῦ καταλόγου τῶν σοφῶν καὶ Μωϋσέα. Λίνον δὲ καὶ Μουσαῖον καὶ Ὀρφέα καὶ τὸν Φερεκύδην καὶ τὸν Πέρσην Ζωροάστρην καὶ Πυθαγόραν φήσας περὶ τῶνδε διειληφέναι. καὶ ἐς βίβλους κατατεθεῖσθαι τὰ ἑαυτῶν δόγματα καὶ πεφυλάχθαι αὐτὰ μέχρι δεῦρο. καὶ ἑκὼν μὲν ἐπελάθετο τοῦ περὶ τῶν νομιζομένων θεῶν μύθου ὡς ἀνθρωποπαθῶν. ἀναγεγραμμένου μάλιστα ὑπὸ Ὀρφέως.
pass_a_gloss: I wonder, how Celsus placed Odrysians and Samothracians and Eleusinians and Hyperboreans among the most ancient and wise nations, but he did not deem the Jews worthy, neither to be received among the wise nor among the ancient; many writings being brought forth by Egyptians and Phoenicians and Greeks, testifying to their antiquity, which I considered superfluous to set forth. For it is possible for one who wishes to read what Flavius Josephus wrote about the antiquity of the Jews in two books, where he brings forth a large collection of writers testifying to the antiquity of the Jews. And also the discourse of Tatian, a younger man, is brought forth against the Greeks, displaying the most learned of those who have written about the antiquity of the Jews and Moses. It seems, therefore, that Celsus speaks these things not truly but with a love of calumny, having as his goal to accuse the origin of Christianity, which is connected to the Jews. But also he says that the Galactophagi of Homer and the Druids of the Gauls and the Getae are most wise and ancient nations, discussing things related to Jewish matters. Of which I do not know if writings are brought forth; but he alone rejects the Hebrews, as far as he is concerned, both from antiquity and from wisdom. Again, making a list of ancient and wise men who have benefited those who came after them and also through writings those who came after them, he excluded Moses from the list of wise men. And of Linus, whom he preferred to those he named, neither laws nor words are brought forth, having turned back and served nations; but the laws of Moses are brought forth by a whole nation, scattered throughout the entire inhabited world. See, therefore, if he did not openly act wickedly by excluding Moses from the list of wise men. He said that Linus and Musaeus and Orpheus and Pherecydes and the Persian Zoroaster and Pythagoras had received these things and had put their own doctrines into books and had preserved them until now. And he willingly forgot the myth about the gods who are considered to be human-like, which was written especially by Orpheus.

choices.why: Celsus' motivation is to accuse Christianity
describing the myth about the gods

pass_b_english: I wonder how Celsus could place the Odrysians, Samothracians, Eleusinians, and Hyperboreans among the most ancient and wise nations, yet refuse to count the Jews as either wise or ancient, even though many writings from Egyptians, Phoenicians, and Greeks testify to their antiquity—writings I considered superfluous to reproduce here. Anyone who wishes can read Flavius Josephus’s two books on the antiquity of the Jews, where he assembles a large collection of authors bearing witness to it, and the younger Tatian’s discourse against the Greeks, which displays the most learned writers on the antiquity of the Jews and Moses. It appears, then, that Celsus speaks these things not in truth but out of a love for calumny, aiming to accuse the origin of Christianity because it is connected to the Jews. He also declares Homer’s Galactophagi, the Druids of the Gauls, and the Getae to be most wise and ancient peoples, discussing matters related to Jewish teachings—peoples of whom I do not know whether any writings survive—while he alone rejects the Hebrews, as far as he can, from both antiquity and wisdom. Again, when compiling a catalogue of ancient and wise men who benefited their contemporaries and later generations through their writings, he expelled Moses from the list of the wise. Of Linus, whom Celsus placed above those he named, neither laws nor words are brought forward that turned back and served nations; but the laws of Moses are carried by a whole nation scattered throughout the entire inhabited world. See, therefore, whether he did not openly act wickedly by excluding Moses from the catalogue of the wise. He claimed that Linus, Musaeus, Orpheus, Pherecydes, the Persian Zoroaster, and Pythagoras had received these things, committed their own doctrines to books, and preserved them until now. And he willingly forgot the myth about the so‑called gods as human‑like, a myth recorded especially by Orpheus.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'φιλαπεχθημόνως' as 'with a love of calumny' (A) and 'out of a love for calumny' (B) correctly captures the sense of the Greek. The list of names and nations is complete and accurate.
